title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
title_zh: 蛋白-配体结合预测中基于结构的方法评估指南
abstract: Scoring functions built with advanced deep learning algorithms have recently gained prominence in protein–ligand pose generation and binding affinity prediction for computational drug design. However, several shortcomings make it increasingly difficult to evaluate scoring functions for a specific task across studies. Transparent disclosure of training data, code and procedures is essential to permit reproducibility, reuse and independent scrutiny. Guarding against data leakage, sampling bias and flawed design is equally important. Meaningful comparisons of scoring functions also require common data splits, checks for run-to-run variability and performance baselines. Here we propose a set of guidelines to help the community identify the most promising methods for addressing these important problems. Ballester and Tran-Nguyen advocate for transparency in data, code and experimental procedures in the evaluation of protein–ligand predictions. They discuss good practices for preventing data leakage and bias, enabling fair, reproducible and meaningful comparisons across different scoring methods.
